characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEOL 2010 microscope; thin foils prepared by twin-jet electropolishing (25% nitric acid in methanol, ~20 V, -30°C)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fe–20% Al deformed 2–3% contains single (1/2)〈111〉 dislocations, generally smoothly curved with some preference for screw orientations; edge dipoles and small dipole loops are trailed from gliding screw dislocations; weak clustering as an incipient cell structure in thicker regions.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Dislocations imaged in Bright Field and Weak Beam modes; planar (shear or thermal) faults observed in various dark field modes; Burgers vectors identified by imaging with a variety of g vectors, generally in Bright Field mode
characterization_methods.purpose: To characterize the dislocation structures produced by straining Fe–20% Al to 2–3% and to identify dislocation Burgers vectors
characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM), Bright Field and Weak Beam imaging

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: TEM micrographs (Fig. 6); scale bars 0.25 µm and 0.2 µm
characterization_methods.key_findings: Curled single dislocations are seen; relative displacement of images (marked d) on reversing the imaging vector confirms the dipole arrangement of many dislocation segments and occasional small loops.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Zone axis (stress axis) [0 1 1]; imaging vector parallel to 011; opposite-sign imaging vectors used for the two photographs
characterization_methods.purpose: To image the curled single dislocations and demonstrate the dipole arrangement of many dislocation segments and loops

characterization_methods.key_findings: Straight, sometimes loosely paired, screw-oriented dislocations coexist with numerous short edge dipole segments and small closed dipole loops attached to/trailing from the straight dislocation lines.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Zone axis near [0 0 1]; imaging g vector 1 1 0 (arrowed)
characterization_methods.purpose: To image straight screw dislocations and the associated edge dipole segments and loops in Fe–20% Al

processing_steps.method: standard induction melting in an alumina crucible under inert gas and drop casting into a 25 mm diameter cylindrical copper mould
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The same Fe–Al base alloy series (including the 20% Al binary) was prepared this way, producing samples with grain size of the order of 0.25 mm; compositions given in atomic percent.

Cooling after solidification was sufficiently slow to allow a high degree of B2 order for alloys rich in Al and a good degree of DO3 order for alloys containing 25–30% Al; the 20% Al alloy is disordered / short-range ordered (confirmed in b0031).

Compression samples cut from the ingots by spark machining, either 3 mm diameter or 5 mm × 5 mm square cross-section, height twice the diameter or width; flat surfaces polished on 1500 grade abrasive paper; nominal strain rate 3×10⁻⁴ s⁻¹; compression axis parallel to the cylinder axis of the cast samples; smooth onset of plasticity with no discrete yield points.

Thin samples were cut from the centre of the deformed samples perpendicular to the stress axis using a diamond saw and thin foils prepared with a twin-jet electropolishing unit using a 25% nitric acid in methanol mixture at about 20 V.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Compression testing to a strain of 2–3%; compression axis parallel to the cylinder axis of the cast samples; smooth onset of plasticity with no discrete yield points and slightly curved stress–strain behaviour.
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: 3 mm diameter or 5 mm × 5 mm square cross-section, height twice the diameter or width

structures.overall_structure: Disordered or short-range-ordered Fe–20% Al deformed 2–3% at room temperature; plasticity is carried by individual, generally smoothly curved single (1/2)〈111〉 dislocations that trail edge dipoles and small dipole loops, with a weak tendency for clustering of dislocations as an incipient cell structure in thick foil regions.

unmapped_findings: Fe–20% Al is disordered or contains some level of short-range order and is deformed by the movement of single dislocations of Burgers vector (1/2)〈111〉, not by superdislocations (b0031, b0063).

The single dislocations in Fe–20% Al are generally smoothly curved (Fig. 6), show some preference for screw orientations (Fig. 7), and in thicker regions of the foils there is some tendency for a weak clustering of dislocations as an incipient cell structure (b0031).

Many of the dislocation segments in the clustered regions and many bowed dislocations in Fe–20% Al are dipoles; the dipole nature of these segments and occasional small loops is confirmed by the relative shift of images on changing from a positive to a negative imaging vector (marked d in Fig. 6) (b0031).
In Fe–20% Al, the edge dipole segments and small dipole loops are produced by trailing from the gliding screw dislocations (b0031, b0032).

For disordered Fe–20% Al there are two reasons for a low work hardening rate: fewer dipoles (curly dislocations of mixed edge and screw character) and the dipole being a single dislocation dipole rather than a super-dislocation (super) dipole (b0055, b0057).
